examples.en: The cup fell on the floor and broke.

examples.ko: 창문이 깨어져서 방 안으로 바람이 들어와요.
examples.en: The window is broken, so wind comes into the room.

examples.ko: 약속이 깨어지면 서로 마음이 많이 아파요.
examples.en: When a promise is broken, both people get hurt.
I carried the plate carefully in case it broke.
The moment the dream was shattered, I felt so empty.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 사이가 깨어지지 않았으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope the relationship between the two of them doesn't break.

explain: '깨지다'와 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때는 줄여서 '깨져요, 깨졌어요'라고 많이 해요. 컵이나 유리 같은 물건뿐 아니라 약속, 꿈, 분위기, 사이가 무너질 때도 써요. 잠에서 '깨다'와는 다른 말이니 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: The cup fell and broke.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깨어졌어요'를 줄인 말로, 말할 때 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The shortened form of '깨어졌어요', used more in speech.

phrases.en: Glass breaks easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 약하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say an object is fragile.

phrases.en: Something suddenly came up, so the plan fell through.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건뿐 아니라 약속이 지켜지지 않을 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not just objects; also used when a promise or plan falls through.

explain_en: It means the same as '깨지다', and in speech people often shorten it to '깨져요' or '깨졌어요'. It is used for objects like cups and glass, and also for promises, dreams, moods and relationships falling apart. Don't confuse it with '깨다' (to wake up from sleep).

examples.en: I was scared because I was left alone at home.
A lot of food has been left over.
The person who is left last turns off the lights.
All that was left to him was an old watch.
All my friends left and only I was left behind.
A note had been left on the desk.

explain: '남다'는 저절로 남는 것이고, '남기다'는 누가 일부러 남기는 것이에요. '남겨지다'는 남기다의 피동으로, 내가 원하지 않았는데 남은 느낌이 강해요. 특히 사람이 혼자 두고 간 곳에 '남겨지다'라고 하면 쓸쓸한 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: A note has been left on the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가 둔 것이 그대로 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something someone left that is still there.

phrases.en: I was the only one left in the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 혼자 남은 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a past situation of being left behind.

phrases.en: I don't want to be left alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하지 않는데 혼자 남는 상황을 싫어한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say you don't want to be left behind against your will.
phrases.en_equiv: don't want to be left behind

explain_en: '남다' is something that remains by itself, and '남기다' is someone deliberately leaving it. '남겨지다' is the passive of 남기다 and feels like being left against your will. Used for a person left alone, it sounds lonely.

examples.en: '책방' and '서점' are synonyms.

examples.ko: 사전에서 동의어를 찾아서 글을 바꿔 썼어요.
examples.en: I found synonyms in the dictionary and rewrote my text.

examples.ko: 한 단어에 동의어가 여러 개 있기도 해요.
examples.en: One word can have several synonyms.

examples.ko: 동의어는 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있지만 느낌이 조금 달라요.
examples.en: Synonyms can replace each other, but the feeling is a little different.

examples.ko: 이 단어의 동의어에는 어떤 것이 있어요?
examples.en: What synonyms does this word have?

examples.ko: 동의어와 반의어를 함께 공부하면 단어가 쉽게 외워져요.
examples.en: If you study synonyms and antonyms together, words are easier to memorize.

explain: 뜻이 같은 말은 동의어, 뜻이 비슷한 말은 '유의어', 뜻이 반대인 말은 '반의어'라고 해요. 한자 '同'은 같다는 뜻이에요. 사전에서는 '비슷한말'이라는 이름으로 나오기도 해요.

phrases.en: I look for synonyms when I write.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 다른 말을 찾을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking for another word with the same meaning.

phrases.en: The two words are similar, but they are not synonyms.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 완전히 같지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the meanings are not exactly the same.

phrases.example: 동의어 사전을 보면 단어를 쉽게 바꿀 수 있어요.
phrases.en: With a synonym dictionary, you can easily swap words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 말을 모아 놓은 책이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A book that collects words with the same meaning.

explain_en: Words with the same meaning are 동의어, words with similar meaning are '유의어', and words with opposite meaning are '반의어'. The character '同' means same. In dictionaries you may also see it listed as '비슷한말'.

en: to be registered; to be enrolled

examples.en: Your member information gets registered.
My name was registered at the school.
A text goes to the registered number.
Once the car is registered, a license plate is issued.
My address has not been registered yet.
I am glad the photo got registered in the app.

explain: 이름, 번호, 차, 회원처럼 공식 명단에 올라갔다는 말이에요. 내가 하면 '등록하다', 올라가 있으면 '등록되다'예요. 학원에 이름을 올릴 때는 '등록하다'를 자주 써요.

phrases.en: This number has not been registered yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명단에 아직 올라가 있지 않다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is not yet on the official list.

phrases.en: I was registered as a library member yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)로 등록되다'로 어떤 자격으로 올라갔는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-(으)로' says in what capacity you were registered.
phrases.en_equiv: to be registered as a member

phrases.example: 등록된 차만 이 주차장에 세울 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Only registered cars can park in this lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '등록된'은 이미 명단에 오른 것을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describes something already on the list.

explain_en: It means a name, number, car or member has been put on an official list. When you do it, it is '등록하다', and when it ends up on the list it is '등록되다'. For signing up at an academy, '등록하다' is common.

examples.en: Beads of sweat formed on my forehead.
The players' sweat dripped onto the floor of the stadium.
I kept running while wiping away the sweat.

examples.ko: 이 금메달은 선수가 흘린 땀방울의 결과예요.
examples.en: This gold medal is the result of the sweat the athlete shed.

examples.ko: 더운 날에는 걷기만 해도 땀방울이 흘러요.
examples.en: On hot days, sweat runs down even if I just walk.
Sweat ran all the way down to the tip of my nose.

explain: 그냥 '땀'보다 방울방울 맺힌 모습이 눈에 보이는 말이에요. '땀방울이 맺히다', '땀방울이 떨어지다'처럼 써요. 노력을 비유할 때도 '땀방울'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: He wiped the beads of sweat from his forehead with his hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: '닦다'와 함께 땀을 없애는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 닦다 it describes wiping the sweat away.

phrases.en: It's hot, so beads of sweat run down my face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땀이 아래로 흘러내리는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes sweat running down.

phrases.en: Beads of sweat drip from my chin.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뚝뚝'과 함께 쓰면 방울이 떨어지는 모습이 잘 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 뚝뚝 you can picture the drops falling.

explain_en: Compared to plain '땀', it makes you picture the sweat as individual drops. It is used as '땀방울이 맺히다' and '땀방울이 떨어지다'. It is also used figuratively for hard effort.

examples.en: They play music from the broadcasting room at lunchtime.

examples.ko: 방송실은 삼 층 복도 끝에 있어요.
examples.en: The broadcasting room is at the end of the hallway on the third floor.

examples.ko: 저는 학교 방송실에서 아침 방송을 맡고 있어요.
examples.en: I am in charge of the morning broadcast in the school broadcasting room.

examples.ko: 방송실 문이 잠겨 있어서 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: The broadcasting room door is locked, so I can't go in.
The teacher told me to come to the broadcasting room.

examples.ko: 방송실에 있는 마이크를 함부로 만지면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not touch the microphone in the broadcasting room carelessly.

explain: 학교나 건물 안에서 안내 방송을 하는 작은 방을 말할 때 많이 써요. 텔레비전이나 라디오를 만드는 큰 곳은 보통 '방송국'이나 '스튜디오'라고 해요.

phrases.en: They make announcements in the broadcasting room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송실 안에서 하는 일을 말할 때 '에서'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 에서 to say what happens inside the broadcasting room.

phrases.example: 우리 학교 방송실은 일 층에 있어요.
phrases.en: Our school's broadcasting room is on the first floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '학교'를 앞에 붙이면 학교 안의 방송실이라는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 학교 makes it clear it is the broadcasting room in a school.

phrases.en: They told me to come to the broadcasting room at lunchtime.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송실로 가거나 오는 방향을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say you go or come to the broadcasting room.

explain_en: It is mostly used for the small room in a school or building where announcements are made. The large place where TV or radio programs are made is usually called a '방송국' or a '스튜디오'.

examples.en: The cat is chasing the mouse.
A mouse is eating the cheese.
In the lab, they do research using mice.
I was startled and hid like a mouse.
The child fed the mouse.
White mice are cute, so they are popular.

explain: '쥐'는 더 넓게 쓰는 말이고, 그중 작은 쥐를 '생쥐'라고 불러요. 실험에 쓰는 쥐를 말할 때도 '생쥐'를 써요.

phrases.example: 비를 맞아서 물에 빠진 생쥐 꼴이에요.
phrases.en: like a mouse that fell in water
phrases.nuance_ko: 비나 물에 흠뻑 젖어서 초라해진 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe someone who is soaking wet and looks bedraggled.

explain_en: 쥐 is the broader word, and the small kind is called 생쥐. The mice used in lab experiments are also called 생쥐.

examples.en: I wrote each Hangul letter ten times in my practice notebook.

examples.ko: 연습장 한 권을 다 쓰고 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: I used up a whole practice notebook and bought a new one.
I solve math problems on scratch paper first.
The notebook ran short, so I wrote on the back pages too.
Can I bring a scratch notebook into the exam room?

examples.ko: 이 연습장은 줄이 없어서 그림 그리기에도 좋아요.
examples.en: This notebook has no lines, so it is good for drawing too.

explain: 연습장은 막 써도 되는 공책이에요. 그림을 그리는 공책은 '스케치북', 수업 내용을 정리하는 공책은 그냥 '공책'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 먼저 연습장에 써 보고 나서 공책에 옮겨요.
phrases.en: I try writing it in a scratch notebook first and then copy it into my notebook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막 써 보는 곳은 '-에'로 말해요. 글씨 연습이나 문제 풀이에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place you write is marked with '-에'; often used for handwriting practice or solving problems.
phrases.en_equiv: to write in a scratch notebook

phrases.example: 수학 문제를 풀려고 연습장 한 권을 샀어요.
phrases.en: I bought a scratch notebook to solve math problems.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공책처럼 '권'으로 세요. '한 권', '두 권'처럼 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Counted with '권' like other notebooks: '한 권', '두 권'.

phrases.en: I needed a new scratch notebook, so I went to the stationery store.
phrases.nuance_ko: '새'는 명사 앞에서 새것이라는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '새' before a noun adds the meaning of 'new'.

explain_en: A 연습장 is a notebook you can scribble in freely. A drawing pad is a '스케치북', and a notebook for class notes is simply a '공책'.

examples.ko: 아기가 우유병을 두 손으로 꼭 잡고 있어요.
examples.en: The baby is holding the milk bottle tightly with both hands.
This milk bottle is light and easy to wash.
I mixed formula in the bottle and gave it to the baby.

examples.ko: 동생이 이제 우유병 대신 컵으로 마셔요.
examples.en: My little brother now drinks from a cup instead of a milk bottle.
I don't know where the milk bottle went.
The baby drinks milk slowly from the bottle.

explain: 아기에게 우유를 먹이는 병을 말해요. 실제로는 '젖병'이라는 말을 더 자주 써요. 소독하다, 씻다, 타다 같은 말과 같이 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: I washed the baby's bottle until it was clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우유병'보다 실제로 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more often in real life than 우유병.

phrases.en: I sterilize the baby bottle in boiling water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기용품을 깨끗하게 할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for cleaning baby items.

phrases.en: I wash the milk bottles every night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 가장 쉽게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The simplest everyday phrase to use with it.

explain_en: This is the bottle used to feed a baby. In real life people more often say '젖병'. It often appears with verbs like 소독하다 (sterilize), 씻다 (wash) and 타다 (mix).

examples.en: The road continues in a straight line.
I drew a straight line in my notebook with a ruler.
The children are standing in a straight line on the playground.
I laid the pencils in a straight line on the desk.
Try connecting the two points with a straight line.

examples.ko: 집에서 학교까지 일직선이라서 길을 잃을 일이 없어요.
examples.en: It is a straight line from home to school, so you cannot get lost.

explain: '직선'과 거의 같지만, 일직선은 '한 줄로 쭉 곧게'라는 느낌이 강해요. 그래서 줄을 서거나 길이 곧게 이어질 때 '일직선으로'를 많이 써요. [일찍썬]으로 읽어요.

phrases.en: If you draw a straight line with a ruler, it looks neat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일직선'과 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 수학이나 그림처럼 선을 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 일직선; used more when talking about lines in math or drawing.

phrases.en: The students are standing in a straight line.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 한 줄로 곧게 설 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when several people stand in one straight row.
phrases.en_equiv: to stand in a straight line

phrases.en: Try walking in a straight line with your eyes closed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옆으로 흔들리지 않고 곧게 걷는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to walk straight without swaying to the side.
phrases.en_equiv: to walk in a straight line

explain_en: It is close to '직선' (straight line), but 일직선 stresses 'one line, perfectly straight'. That is why '일직선으로' is common for lining up or for a road running straight. It is read [일찍썬].

examples.en: Photos are saved on the phone automatically.

examples.ko: 파일이 저장되지 않아서 다시 만들어야 해요.
examples.en: The file wasn't saved, so I have to make it again.

examples.ko: 이 번호는 제 전화에 저장돼 있어요.
examples.en: This number is saved on my phone.
There was no saved password, so I typed it in myself.

examples.ko: 제 숙제가 지금 클라우드에 저장되고 있어요.
examples.en: The homework is being saved to the cloud.

examples.ko: 모두 저장되는 데 시간이 조금 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a little time for everything to be saved.

explain: '저장하다'는 내가 버튼을 누르는 행동이고, '저장되다'는 화면에 '저장되었습니다'가 뜰 때처럼 결과 상태예요. 번호, 사진, 파일에 자주 써요. 번호를 누르는 건 '입력하다', 연락처에 넣는 건 '저장하다'예요.

phrases.example: 그 번호는 제 휴대폰에 저장돼 있어요.
phrases.en: That number is saved in my phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 들어 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something already stored.

phrases.en: The internet is slow, so it won't save.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저장하려 해도 되지 않을 때 일상 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in conversation when saving fails.

phrases.en: My friend's phone number was saved in my contacts.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어디에'를 넣어서 저장된 장소를 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'where' tells the place something is saved.

explain_en: 저장하다 is the action of pressing the button, and 저장되다 is the resulting state, like when 저장되었습니다 appears on screen. It is used with numbers, photos, and files. Typing digits is 입력하다, and putting them in contacts is 저장하다.

examples.en: In the old days, rice or shells were used like money.
I picked up pretty shells at the beach.

examples.ko: 조개껍데기에 귀를 대면 파도 소리가 나는 것 같아요.
examples.en: If you hold a shell to your ear, it sounds like waves.
The child made a necklace out of shells.

examples.ko: 조개껍데기 안에 작은 게가 숨어 있었어요.
examples.en: A small crab was hiding inside the shell.

examples.ko: 모래 위에 조개껍데기가 여기저기 흩어져 있어요.
examples.en: Shells are scattered here and there on the sand.

explain: '껍데기'는 조개나 달걀처럼 딱딱한 겉을 말하고, 과일이나 양파처럼 벗겨 내는 부드러운 겉은 보통 '껍질'이라고 해요. 조개는 '조개껍질'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The child collects shells at the beach.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조개껍데기'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is used with the same meaning as 'jogae-kkeopdegi'.

phrases.en: Every time I travel, I collect shells.
phrases.nuance_ko: 취미로 모을 때 '모으다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '모으다' is used when collecting as a hobby.

phrases.en: My friend gave me a shell necklace as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조개껍데기로 만든 물건 이름 앞에 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put it before the name of an item made from shells.

explain_en: '껍데기' is for hard outsides such as shellfish or eggs, while the softer peel of fruit or onions is usually called '껍질'. A shell is also called '조개껍질'.

examples.en: I caught a cold and my nostrils are blocked.
Don't pick your nose in front of people.

examples.ko: 아이가 콧구멍에 콩을 넣어서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: The child put a bean in its nostril, so we went to the hospital.
Try breathing slowly through your nostrils.
A person has two nostrils.
When I wash my face, I clean my nostrils well too.

explain: '코'와 '구멍' 사이에 'ㅅ'이 들어가 '콧구멍'이 돼요. 발음은 [코꾸멍]이에요. '콧물'도 같은 방식으로 만들어진 말이에요.

phrases.en: A horse has really big nostrils.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양이나 크기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about shape or size.

phrases.en: My nostrils are blocked because of the cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 콧구멍으로 숨쉬기 힘들 때 써요. 일상에서는 '코가 막히다'도 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it is hard to breathe through the nose. In daily talk, '코가 막히다' is also common.

phrases.en: I put medicine in both nostrils.
phrases.nuance_ko: 콧구멍은 두 개라서 '양쪽'과 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: There are two, so it's often used with '양쪽'.

explain_en: An 'ㅅ' is inserted between '코' and '구멍' to form '콧구멍', pronounced [코꾸멍]. '콧물' is formed the same way.

en: to be wrapped; to be gift-wrapped; to be packed

examples.en: The gift has been wrapped prettily.

examples.ko: 이 과자는 한 개씩 포장돼 있어요.
examples.en: These snacks are packed one by one.

examples.ko: 포장된 음식은 집에서 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Packed food can be eaten at home.
If you order, it arrives safely packed in a box.

examples.ko: 길이 새로 포장되면 차가 편하게 다녀요.
examples.en: Once the road is newly paved, cars can travel comfortably.

examples.ko: 포장되지 않은 길은 비 오면 위험해요.
examples.en: An unpaved road is dangerous when it rains.

explain: 물건이 상자나 종이에 싸인 상태를 말해요. 식당에서 음식을 싸 갈 때 '포장해 주세요'는 사람이 하는 일이라 '포장하다'를 써요. '포장되다'는 길에 아스팔트를 깔았다는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.example: 과자가 한 봉지씩 따로 포장돼 있어요.
phrases.en: The snacks are packed separately, one bag each.
phrases.nuance_ko: '따로'를 붙여 하나씩 나누어 싸 두었다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '따로' means each item is wrapped separately.

phrases.en: The village road was newly paved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길에 아스팔트를 깔았다는 뜻으로도 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: It can also mean a road was paved.

phrases.example: 이 빵은 포장되지 않아서 바로 먹어야 해요.
phrases.en: This bread isn't wrapped, so you should eat it right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 싸지 않고 그대로 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something left as it is, without wrapping.

explain_en: It describes an item being wrapped in a box or paper. When you ask a restaurant '포장해 주세요', a person does the action, so '포장하다' is used. '포장되다' is also used for a road that has been paved.

en: to be displayed; to be indicated; to be marked

examples.en: The time is shown on the screen.
The tax is shown on the price tag.

examples.ko: 지도에 우리 집이 빨간 점으로 표시됐어요.
examples.en: Our house was marked with a red dot on the map.
Please wait at the marked spot.
The message is not marked as read.

examples.ko: 이 앱에는 날씨가 숫자로 표시되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I wish this app showed the weather as numbers.

explain: 눈으로 볼 수 있게 화면이나 종이에 나타난다는 말이에요. 앱, 지도, 가격표처럼 정보를 보여 줄 때 자주 나와요. 내가 직접 나타내면 '표시하다', 나타나 있으면 '표시되다'예요.

phrases.en: The price is marked on the product.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 적혀 있어서 지금 볼 수 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something already shown and visible now.

phrases.en: My home's location is shown on the map.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앱 지도에서 장소가 나타날 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when a place appears on a map app.
phrases.en_equiv: to be marked on a map

phrases.en: I mark the important parts with color.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 직접 나타낼 때 써요. 나타나 있으면 '표시되다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person does the marking. When it simply appears, use '표시되다'.

explain_en: It means information appears on a screen or paper where you can see it, and it is common with apps, maps and price tags. When you do it yourself it is '표시하다', and when it appears it is '표시되다'.

examples.en: Grandfather reads the newspaper sitting in a wheelchair.

examples.ko: 휠체어가 들어갈 수 있는 엘리베이터가 있어요.
examples.en: There is an elevator a wheelchair can enter.

examples.ko: 다리를 다쳐서 한 달 동안 휠체어로 다녔어요.
examples.en: I hurt my leg and got around in a wheelchair for a month.
There is a separate wheelchair space on the bus.

examples.ko: 친구의 휠체어를 밀어 주면서 같이 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked together with my friend, pushing his wheelchair.
A wheelchair cannot be used on stairs.

explain: '휠체어를 타다'와 '휠체어에 앉다'를 둘 다 써요. 사람을 말할 때는 '휠체어를 타는 분'처럼 정중하게 말하는 게 좋아요.

phrases.en: I hurt my leg, so I get around in a wheelchair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휠체어로 이동한다고 할 때 '타다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 타다 when you move around by wheelchair.

phrases.en: I'll push your wheelchair, grandma.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 앉은 휠체어를 밀어 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you push a wheelchair that someone else is sitting in.

phrases.en: An electric wheelchair moves with a button.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전기로 움직이는 휠체어를 말할 때 앞에 '전동'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 전동 before it for a wheelchair that runs on electricity.

explain_en: Both '휠체어를 타다' and '휠체어에 앉다' are used. When talking about a person, it is polite to say '휠체어를 타는 분'.
